validity.researcher_notes: Tested per the brief's instruction: does P6011 Project Maple (2023, Ramapo NY/Salem MA receipt-point capacity additions, 750,000 Dth/d, in-service as early as Nov 2029) re-scope the cancelled P0144 Access Northeast (a much larger, earlier ~2015-2018 Algonquin/Enbridge New England expansion that was cancelled after New England states declined to fund it via electric ratepayer contracts)? No primary or secondary source found this session states Project Maple is a revival, continuation, or re-scoping of Access Northeast — Enbridge's own Open Season Notice for Project Maple does not mention Access Northeast at all, and describes Project Maple as new receipt-point capacity work (looping/larger-diameter pipe/added compression at EXISTING Algonquin facilities) framed as a fresh 2023 proposal, not a resurrection of the earlier project. The two differ in scope framing, receipt points, and capacity mechanics (Access Northeast bundled a large compressor buildout tied to New England utility RFPs; Project Maple is scoped around the Ramapo NY and Salem MA receipt points only). Given a search of Enbridge's own materials and independent press turned up no explicit linkage, the working finding is 'no evidence of a stated revival relationship' rather than a confident denial — flagged here and as a cross-row lead for whoever is sweeping P0144, since that row's own sources should be checked for any claim in the other direction.

validity.researcher_notes: EIA DATA-CONFLATION FINDING: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset lists 'Project Maple' identically across every release from 2024-04 through 2026-01 (beg_state=NY, end_state=MA, additional_capacity_mmcf_d=750, year_in_service_date=2029) — consistent with GEM's own recorded values. The 2026-05 release renames the SAME row to 'Algonquin Reliable Affordable Resilient Enhancement (formerly Project Maple)' and adds docket_number=PF26-7-000, while carrying forward the identical NY/MA/750/2029 figures unchanged. However, the actual FERC docket PF26-7-000 — per the Federal Register's own Notice of Scoping Period (published 2026-06-09, document 2026-11538) for 'Algonquin Reliable Affordable Resilient Enhancement (RARE)' — describes a physically DIFFERENT, much smaller project: approximately 13.5 miles of new pipeline entirely within Middlesex County, Connecticut and Worcester/Norfolk Counties, Massachusetts and Newport/Providence Counties, Rhode Island, plus modifications at the Cromwell Compressor Station (Connecticut) — with NO New York component anywhere in the notice. This is an EIA row-mislabeling/conflation error (the analyst renamed an old row onto a new docket without updating the geography/capacity fields), not evidence that GEM's P6011 record is stale or wrong. P6011's Capacity/StartYear1 values are retained as-is; this caveat is recorded so a future sweep does not 'correct' P6011 using the EIA 2026-05 relabeling.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Annual-update status review: Project Maple was announced/open-season'd September-November 2023 seeking binding shipper commitments for 750,000 Dth/d of new capacity at the Ramapo (NY) and Salem (MA) receipt points, targeting in-service 'as early as November 2029'. Checked for progress or reversal: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects dataset shows status='Announced' consistently across all 8 releases from 2024-04 through 2026-01 (30+ months of no status change) — no FID, no construction, no cancellation recorded; (2) no FERC pre-filing (PF) or certificate (CP) docket was found under 'Project Maple' specifically; (3) the ONLY FERC docket found under a similar Algonquin New England banner, PF26-7-000 ('Algonquin Reliable Affordable Resilient Enhancement', opened Feb 2026, Federal Register notice 2026-06-09), is a physically DIFFERENT, smaller CT/MA/RI-only project per the validity[] EIA-conflation finding — it does not represent Project Maple advancing to pre-filing; (4) no news coverage found (through the WBUR/nocompressor articles, both Sept 2023) reports withdrawal or abandonment. Given US pipeline projects in early open-season stages routinely take 2+ years before any FERC filing, and 2023-2026 is within that normal range with no adverse signal, this is a 'confirm' rather than 'stale' — the project is dormant in the sense of no NEW milestones, but not stalled beyond what is typical for a project whose in-service target (Nov 2029) is still ~3 years further out. Recommend GEM's next annual check specifically verify whether a FERC pre-filing docket has since opened under the Project Maple name (distinct from PF26-7-000/RARE).
